findings.doc_quote: The field sits under [hassette.lifecycle] in hassette.toml and defaults to 30 seconds.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/config/models.py:35 — `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10`; models.py:335 — `shutdown_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, gt=0)`; src/hassette/config/hassette.prod.toml:9 — `shutdown_timeout_seconds = 10`; src/hassette/config/hassette.dev.toml:9 — `shutdown_timeout_seconds = 20`
findings.explanation: The model default and the prod defaults file are both 10 seconds, and the dev defaults file sets 20. No default is 30 seconds.
findings.suggested_fix: The field sits under [hassette.lifecycle] in hassette.toml and defaults to 10 seconds.

findings.doc_quote: A stop whose hook timed out is reported STOPPED with a "timed out" reason, even when the hook ended as soon as it was cancelled.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/core/app_lifecycle_instances.py:215 — docstring: `A stop whose hook timed out but left nothing running: FAILED with a "timed out" reason; reloadable.`; :275 — `timed_out = force_terminated or outcome.result is ShutdownResult.TIMED_OUT`; :377-382 — builds `TimeoutError(f"stop of app '{name}' timed out after {friendly_time}")`, calls `record_failure`, then `outcomes.failed`; :292 — `send_outcome_event(inst, status=FAILED, previous_status=STOPPING, exception=exc)`; src/hassette/core/app_registry.py:111-117 — `record_failure` stores `status=ResourceStatus.FAILED`
findings.explanation: A timed-out hook produces a TIMED_OUT outcome. shutdown_instance then skips the STOPPED branch, records a failure entry, and emits a FAILED event. The instance's own Resource status ends at STOPPED, but the registry entry and the app state event both report FAILED.
findings.suggested_fix: A stop whose hook timed out is reported FAILED with a "timed out" reason, even when the hook ended as soon as it was cancelled.

findings.doc_quote: Before the shutdown hooks run, Hassette cancels all bus subscriptions created via self.bus , all scheduled jobs created via self.scheduler , and all background tasks tracked by self.task_bucket .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/resources/base.py:631-638 — `run_hooks(self, [self.before_shutdown, self.on_shutdown, self.after_shutdown], ...)` runs first, then `tail_outcome = await self._run_post_hook_shutdown_stage()`; base.py:479 — that stage starts with `_run_task_bucket_shutdown_stage()`; base.py:507 — `_shutdown_children()`; src/hassette/bus/bus.py:184-189 — `Bus.on_shutdown` calls `remove_all_listeners()`; src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:185-188 — `Scheduler.on_shutdown` calls `remove_all_jobs()`
findings.explanation: The order is the reverse of what the page says. The app's shutdown hooks run first. Task bucket cancellation and the Bus and Scheduler child shutdowns happen afterward, so subscriptions, jobs and tasks are still live while the hooks run. App does not override _shutdown_body.
findings.suggested_fix: After the shutdown hooks complete, Hassette cancels all bus subscriptions created via self.bus, all scheduled jobs created via self.scheduler, and all background tasks tracked by self.task_bucket.

findings.doc_quote: attempting to override any of them raises CannotOverrideFinalError when the app is first instantiated.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/resources/base.py:47-85 — the check is in the metaclass: `class FinalMeta(type)`, `def __init__(cls, name, bases, ns, **kw)`, `raise CannotOverrideFinalError(method_name, origin_name, subclass_name, suggested_alt, loc)`. A probe calling `type('Badinitialize', (App,), {...})` raised for initialize, shutdown and cleanup with no instance created.
findings.explanation: The error is raised when the subclass is defined, which is at module import, not at instantiation. Line 50 of the same page correctly says class load time.
findings.suggested_fix: attempting to override any of them raises CannotOverrideFinalError at class load time.

findings.doc_quote: Hassette runs each variant in a thread pool via task_bucket.to_thread , so blocking calls do not stall the event loop.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/app/app.py:330 — `await self.task_bucket.run_in_thread(self.on_initialize_sync)`, and the same call at :310, :315, :320, :325, :335; src/hassette/task_bucket/task_bucket.py:312 — `def run_in_thread(self, fn, *args, **kwargs)`. `grep to_thread src/hassette/task_bucket/` finds only a comment at task_bucket.py:542 about anyio's `to_thread.run_sync`.
findings.explanation: TaskBucket has no to_thread method. The AppSync hooks delegate through task_bucket.run_in_thread.
findings.suggested_fix: Hassette runs each variant in a thread pool via task_bucket.run_in_thread, so blocking calls do not stall the event loop.

findings.doc_quote: The .sync facades provide synchronous access from _sync hooks: self.bus.sync , self.scheduler.sync , self.api.sync , and self.states.sync .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/bus/bus.py:144,158, src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:122,151 and src/hassette/api/api.py:247,262 each declare and create a `sync` facade. `grep '\bsync\b\|Sync' src/hassette/state_manager/` finds none on StateManager, and a probe of `hasattr(StateManager, 'sync')` returned False. src/hassette/state_manager/state_manager.py:311 — `__getattr__` treats the name as a domain; :353-357 — raises `AttributeError(f"Domain '{domain}' is not registered in the state registry...")`
findings.explanation: StateManager has no sync facade. self.states.sync falls into the domain lookup in __getattr__, which raises AttributeError unless a domain named 'sync' is registered. The bus, scheduler and api facades do exist. This finding comes from reading the code path and the class-level probe; self.states.sync was not called on a live instance.
findings.suggested_fix: The .sync facades provide synchronous access from _sync hooks: self.bus.sync, self.scheduler.sync, and self.api.sync.

summary: IMPORTANT: all six findings are in text that exists only in this briefing, because docs/pages/core-concepts/apps/lifecycle.md (worktree HEAD fca419b3) and the extracted pages/core-concepts--apps--lifecycle.txt both have the correct wording on those five lines (10 seconds, FAILED, After the shutdown hooks complete, class load time, run_in_thread, no self.states.sync), and `git log -G` finds neither 'first instantiated' nor 'Before the shutdown hooks run' in the file's history, so check how the briefing was generated before editing the page. Judged as written, the briefing has six errors, clustered in the shutdown section and the AppSync details. Every other checked claim passed against the code, including hook order, failed-init handling and skipped shutdown hooks, the final-method rules, and the needs-restart behavior, so the on-disk page shows no accuracy findings on the claims checked.
